description: Add the cross-contract Video validation helper (VideoOverlayManifestBridge) and the atomic, revision-consistent persistence of runtimeTrack + OverlayManifest. This is the data/validation layer that guarantees a manifested revision is either fully installed (track + manifest + revision metadata all durable) or the prior valid revision stays entirely intact — never a mixed revision. No regie/UI wiring yet; this feature is pure, JVM-testable logic plus its unit tests (sections 5, 6, 20-B, 20-C).
steps: Create VideoOverlayManifestBridge.java in app/src/main/java/com/scenevibe/tvcompanionpoc/. Give it a pure static (or instance, no Android deps) method that takes a parsed ScheduledTrack (runtimeTrack) and a parsed OverlayManifest and returns a bounded validation result (ok / failure-with-bounded-code). Enforce EXACTLY (section 5): manifest.product=='video'; manifest.sourceId.equals(runtimeTrack.trackId); manifest.clockMode=='media'; each runtimeTrack comment.id maps to exactly one manifest scene.id (bijection); no extra Video scenes; for each matched pair scene.startMs == comment.startMs AND scene.durationMs == comment.durationMs compared as exact integer milliseconds (long ==). On any failure return a bounded failure; never include comment/scene text in the result or any log. Keep this logic OUT of CloudControlClient.

Build a scene index by id inside the bridge (or a small helper the regie will reuse later) so the mapping check is O(n) and reusable. Index must detect duplicate scene ids and missing/extra ids distinctly enough to pick the right bounded diagnostic (MANIFEST_INCONSISTENT vs MANIFEST_INVALID).

Add bounded diagnostic codes needed here to RuntimeDiagnostics (adapt to the existing enum style used by CloudErrorCode/MediaIdentityState): MANIFEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_INCONSISTENT, MANIFEST_CACHE_FAILED. Wire them into DiagnosticsStore observational setters following the existing observational-only pattern (never gate logic, never log content/secrets). Read RuntimeDiagnostics.java and DiagnosticsStore.java first to match the exact enum/setter conventions.

Extend durable persistence so runtimeTrack + manifest share one revision atomically. Audit CloudTrackRepository.Storage first. Prefer the minimal additive change: extend the Storage interface save to also carry the manifest JSON (e.g. add a save(long revision, String runtimeJson, String manifestJson) or a parallel key), OR add a new OverlayManifestRepository that writes through the SAME SharedPreferences editor commit so the write is one atomic .commit(). The invariant: a successful install persists revision + runtime + manifest together; a failed/invalid manifest install must NOT replace the prior runtime+manifest+revision. There must be no code path that leaves runtimeTrack at revision N and manifest at revision N-1. Keep the existing Context ctor (real SharedPreferences.commit) and the injectable Storage ctor (JVM tests). Keep legacy Case A (no manifest) persistence behavior byte-for-byte unchanged: an assignment without a manifest persists exactly as today and stores no manifest.

Add a restore path that returns, atomically, both the runtimeTrack (loaded into the scheduler as today) and the active manifest (parsed and validated on restore; corruption of EITHER fails closed to the whole revision being discarded — never a half-restore). Corruption must never reach the scheduler or regie.

Add JVM tests. Extend/add tests covering section 20-B (cases 4-10): trackId==sourceId pass; comment ids == scene ids pass; a missing id => reject; an extra scene => reject; startMs mismatch => reject; durationMs mismatch => reject; a product/clock mismatch => reject; and that a reject yields a bounded failure (no ACK is produced by the bridge — bridge has no ACK responsibility, assert it returns failure). Section 20-C (cases 11-15): runtime+manifest persisted at the same revision; restore after a fresh repository instance returns the same revision with both runtime and manifest; corrupt manifest in storage => fail closed (whole revision discarded, scheduler untouched); a new INVALID revision does not replace a prior valid revision; assert there is never a mixed revision (install of a bad manifest leaves BOTH runtime and manifest at the prior revision). Reuse the Memory Storage test double and manifest fixture builders from CloudTrackRepositoryTest / OverlayManifestParserTest patterns.
acceptance_criteria: VideoOverlayManifestBridge exists, is Android-independent (JVM-testable, no android.* imports), and enforces all section-5 rules with exact integer-ms comparison and a comment.id<->scene.id bijection.
A new or extended repository persists runtimeTrack + manifest + revision atomically; no code path can produce a mixed revision; legacy no-manifest persistence is unchanged.
Restore returns both runtimeTrack and a validated manifest for the same revision, or fails closed to discard the whole revision; corruption never reaches scheduler/regie.
New JVM tests cover section 20-B cases 4-10 and 20-C cases 11-15 and pass under :app:testDebugUnitTest.
No ACK protocol change; no new Android permission; CloudControlClient does not contain the cross-contract logic.
verification: <gradle8.9> :app:testDebugUnitTest --console=plain (new bridge + cache tests pass, existing CloudTrackRepositoryTest/OverlayManifestParserTest still pass)
findings:
Implemented FEAT-002 fully; all gates green.

Files added:
- app/src/main/java/com/scenevibe/tvcompanionpoc/VideoOverlayManifestBridge.java: pure, Android-independent cross-contract Video validator (section 5). Enforces product=='video', clockMode=='media', sourceId.equals(trackId); builds an O(n) scene-id index that detects duplicate scene ids (MANIFEST_INVALID); requires equal cardinality + a comment.id<->scene.id bijection with no extra scenes (MANIFEST_INCONSISTENT); compares startMs/durationMs as exact long == (MANIFEST_INCONSISTENT on any 1ms drift). Returns a bounded Result{ok,code} carrying only a ManifestCode, never comment/scene content, and has no ACK responsibility. Logic kept OUT of CloudControlClient.
- app/src/test/java/.../VideoOverlayManifestBridgeTest.java: section 20-B cases 4-10 (match pass, sourceId mismatch, missing id, extra scene, startMs mismatch, durationMs mismatch, product/clock mismatch), each asserting a bounded failure code and no ACK.
- app/src/test/java/.../CloudManifestCacheTest.java: section 20-C cases 11-15 plus a cache-failure case and a legacy Case A guard. Uses a Memory Storage double whose manifest-aware save mirrors the single-commit SharedPreferences semantics.

Files modified:
- RuntimeDiagnostics.java: added bounded ManifestCode enum {NONE, MANIFEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_INCONSISTENT, MANIFEST_CACHE_FAILED} (mirrors CloudErrorCode style), a lastManifestCode field + builder method, and wired observed.lastManifestCode() into capture(). Observational only.
- DiagnosticsStore.java: added observational setLastManifestCode/lastManifestCode (bounded enum, never content/secrets) following the existing setter pattern; included it in resetCloudObservations().
- CloudTrackRepository.java: added Storage.save(long,String,String) as a default method (keeps legacy test doubles compiling) that commits revision+runtime+manifest in ONE atomic .commit(); the real Context ctor overrides it and the legacy save(long,String) now also remove()s any stale manifest key in the same commit so Case A stores no manifest and never keeps an older revision's manifest. Added install(revision,runtimeJson,manifestJson,scheduler) -> InstallResult (validates runtime + manifest + bridge, commits atomically, loads scheduler only on full success; any failure leaves the prior revision entirely intact -> no mixed revision) and restoreWithManifest(scheduler) -> RestoreResult (requires valid runtime AND cross-checked manifest at the same revision; corruption of either fails closed, clears storage, scheduler untouched; a non-manifested revision returns a failed result WITHOUT clearing so legacy restore() remains the Case A authority).

Scope kept tight: no regie/OverlayService/CloudControlClient/ACK wiring (FEAT-003/004). Legacy install(long,String,scheduler) and restore(scheduler) signatures and behavior preserved; existing CloudTrackRepositoryTest/CloudResetTest/CloudResetAsyncTest untouched and still green. No new Android permission, no WebView/JS/dynamic loading, no manifest package/version/signing/ACK changes.
